newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH COALITION STRAINED OVER MINISTER'S SACKING.
newsitem.headline: POLISH COALITION STRAINED OVER MINISTER'S SACKING.

text.p: Poland's Peasant party (PSL) accused its larger ex-communist partner on Thursday of sacking a Peasant minister in a bid to sabotage their two-party ruling coalition and force early elections.

"The Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) is declaring war on the PSL," a Peasant parliamentary leader, Janusz Piechocinski said in an angry reaction to Wednesday's sudden firing of his party colleague Jacek Buchacz from the foreign trade ministry.
A another senior PSL official, Aleksander Bentkowski, told Gazeta Wyborcza newspaper: "After such a humiliation, we might quit the government"
"If the coalition breaks up, we will have early elections in spring. This is very likely," he said.
The government said on Wednesday Jacek Buchacz had been dismissed by the president, on a motion from SLD Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, after official investigations.

It gave no details but said the probes concerned "involvement of the treasury in ventures concerning export guarantees, in which state and private property is connected in a way that lacks sufficient clarity."
Buchacz and fellow (PSL) leaders charged that the prime minister's SLD had not even told them in advance of the move.
Buchacz himself told a news conference: "I regard my dismissal...as a clear breaking of the coalition agreement."
PSL chiefs briefly held talks with the SLD leadership on Wednesday but broke them off, saying their own party would meet on Friday to decide whether to resume the discussions.

The PSL's Piechocinski, speaking on private Radio Zet, said the sacking of Buchacz aimed to provoke his party to break the coalition, so the SLD could form a minority government backed by its former chief, the President Aleksander Kwasniewski.
It could then call early parliamentary elections, not otherwise due until September 1997, by April next year.
Piechocinski said he would suggest a meeting of both parliamentary parties on Tuesday to thrash out the issue.
An SLD leader, Jerzy Szmajdzinski, called the allegations "science fiction," and said his party did not aim to bust the coalition.
He said the PSL could propose another member to replace Buchacz, whose post is now temporarily held by deputy minister Janusz Kaczurba, and this candidate would be appointed.

Szmajdzinski said the issue was only about Buchacz, who had defied cabinet orders to wait for concrete guidelines and instead gone ahead with actions involving "an outflow of capital from the treasury to private structures."
The exact allegations against Buchacz, revealed in inspections by official oversight bodies, were not revealed.
Earlier this year the government rejected plans by Buchacz to set up a new export guarantee system.
Buchacz has formed some treasury-controlled companies to which, as treasury representative, he allocated shares still retained by the state after privatisations of other firms.
The newly-created companies were designed to provide export guarantees or to invest in private or other state-owned firms.

Piechocinski conceded Buchacz should explain his actions, but said the minister had been trying to boost exports and prevent Poland's official foreign trade deficit from reaching $10 billion by end-1996. It was $1.8 billion last year.

The coalition has linked the two parties rooted in the old communist system, through two cabinet reshuffles and several major rows, since the 1993 polls in which they defeated parties stemming from the pre-1989 anti-communist Solidarity movement. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
